quest.title: Time for the Showdown
quest.description: In the distant skies, far from the surface, the airborne workshop bears silent witness to the amassing and annihilation of obsession...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x475, Primogem x60, Mora x38100, Guide to Conflict x5, The Cornerstone of Stars and Flames x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.num: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Act III
chapter.title: Guns and Wings

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Here it is, the workshop in the sky... You gotta see it to believe it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Makes you wonder why Tepal even bothers with Phlogiston Wings when he has tech like this.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Well, according to the notebook, the platform beneath us runs on components from the Cinder City. Those can't be mass-produced.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Also, I have some doubts about its mobility after seeing how it moved just now...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: For someone like Tepal, who dreams of flying freely, this definitely doesn't cut it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But if he's got that relic, he should be able to make a set of prototype Wings for himself, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why bother making a whole flying workshop so he can mass-produce them?

choices.text: If he can come and go freely from this workshop...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But this doesn't add up... If he's already achieved the power of flight, then he must have bigger dreams we don't know about. But what?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: With any luck, we'll find the answers in his workshop.

choices.text: He's probably already built those prototype Wings for himself.

dialogues.speaker: Chime
dialogues.text: Cheep...

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: Cheep!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chime!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Allpa!

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Careful, don't make any rash decisions... Unless you want to see her suffer.

dialogues.speaker: Chime
dialogues.text: Cheep!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... That's one of the extraction cages!

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: I told my subordinates to take control of the tribe while I was away. Luckily for them... our strongest warrior and our most powerful ally aren't there to stop it.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Take control...? What are you planning to do with Mutota and his supporters!?

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Merely accelerate their inevitable downfall — they cannot stand in the way of progress forever... It is not the move I wished to make, but I'm afraid you and your friends forced my hand.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: And since you insist on opposing me too, I have no choice but to keep you here until the dust has settled.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hah, so that's what you meant by, "I just want to talk." You never intended to negotiate, you just wanted to stall us.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: No, Chasca, I genuinely hoped I could win you over.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: You are the strongest warriors we have. Put down your weapons, and I promise you that no harm will come to this young saurian.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: I just need you to stay here for the next couple of weeks or so, while my people consolidate their power. Then, I will give her back to you, and you'll be free to leave.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You really think the Pyro Archon is gonna let you get away with a coup?

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: ...As long as the majority supports our vision, even the Pyro Archon cannot meddle in our internal affairs.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Your vision is deranged... and the Flower-Feather Clan will never support it!

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: You sure about that? Then wait here and see. Time will tell.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do we do? Even if the whole tribe fights back, Mutota's in grave danger...

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Stop delaying the inevitable. Drop your weapons and get into the cages. Now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... She's still holding Chime hostage... Is there really no other way?

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: (I'm sorry, Chime...)

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: (I might have to do something... unmotherly.)

dialogues.speaker: Chime
dialogues.text: (...Do it, Mom.)

dialogues.speaker: Chime
dialogues.text: (I don't want to be a burden... What kind of warrior would that make me?)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Coya...?

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Huh? What are you yapping about?

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: ...Stand down. Drop your weapons, now! This instant!

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Ugh... Aah!

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: No! The relic...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Now!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Coya! Are you hurt? Let me take a look at you!

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: Cheep...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "I'm fine?" Didn't I tell you to catch me on your back? Why did you try to shield me from the blast!?

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: Cheep...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: "Accident"? Yeah, right! ...Seriously, you're as stubborn as ever...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chasca! Coya!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hah... How are things looking here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All taken care of.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All it took was a little DIY...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...I think that's putting it mildly.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I owe you one... Again.

dialogues.speaker: Chime
dialogues.text: Cheep...

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: Cheep...

dialogues.speaker: Chime
dialogues.text: Cheep...?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...Allpa, be honest. Do you still think qucusaurs can't form bonds?

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: ...Mom, I'll figure out the refinement problem. I'll find a way.

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: ...You don't need to worry about it.

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: ...I just need some more time, that's all I ask... Please, just trust me. Just this once.

dialogues.speaker: Chime
dialogues.text: Cheep!

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: Cheep!

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: The Flower-Feather Clan yields to the strong... and it's up to the winners to define what "strength" means.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: So it looks like... it's my turn to yield.

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: Cheep...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Coya? ...Coya!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why won't it fly away like the others? Is it...

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: ...Cheep.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...She's still breathing, but barely.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: By the looks of it... Tepal was using these cages to extract phlogiston from the qucusaurs.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Once a qucusaur is drained of phlogiston, it becomes too weak to move... We'll have to come back for these ones after dealing with Tepal.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's another notebook here.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Let me see... Looks like a record of his phlogiston research.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Log No. 330. With the support of ██, I was finally able to launch the airborne workshop.

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: Even though it relies on the relic for eighty percent of its power supply, I've at least taken the first step.

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: Log No. 348. Research on the relic is progressing well. I should be able to replicate the technology and scale up production very soon.

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: ██ has proposed a name for this groundbreaking invention: the "Phlogiston Wings"... I think I'm getting close. Soon, I will achieve my dreams!

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: Log No. 377. Encountered some issues with the new smaller-model Phlogiston Wings. The gaseous phlogiston showed some volatility during the refinement process.

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: ██ thinks we should proceed at a more cautious pace with the refinement experiments... But after so many past failures, I have to prove that I will succeed this time.

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: Log No. 114. Ran an experiment using qucusaurs to refine gaseous phlogiston. It was a success.

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: Log No. 117. I have started recruiting merchants and hunters to capture wild qucusaurs.

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: Log No. 121. Major breakthrough in the efficiency of phlogiston yield...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... So many parts have been crossed out!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Yeah, probably the contact he alluded to in his other notebook... Guess he has a benefactor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, did anyone else notice how the numbering system in this notebook suddenly changed half way through?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, and the tone seemed to change a lot, too...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: We haven't got time for textual analysis, I'm afraid. Grab the notebook and let's press on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look here! More of Tepal's notes!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's hope there's some useful information inside.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You scour Tepal's notes for info...

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: Log No. 403. ██ introduced me to some new comrades who fully support my ideas.

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: I told them that some saurians are blessed with wings, and some people with natural gifts, while the less fortunate among us can only look on longingly as they seize the skies...

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: But I also told them that progress can erase individual differences. Think of the tools humanity has made to fight back against wild beasts, the law we have put in place to even the playing field between the strong and the weak...

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: I promised them that our research will be the new frontier of human progress. With our Phlogiston Wings, the power of flight will no longer be for a select few to enjoy. Imagine a world where the skies are for all to share!

dialogues.speaker: Tepal
dialogues.text: I only hope that when we finally achieve this goal... ██ will be proud of me.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: "Imagine a world where the skies are for all to share"... Yes, what a wonderful world that would be...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: If only it were possible. We could respond faster... and so many tragedies could be prevented.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But Tepal... What about the saurians you're draining dry of phlogiston?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You're not sharing the sky... You're stealing it!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Bad move... I won't let you get away with it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Chasca...?

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: Cheep...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'm fine. Let's keep moving — I don't think we'll find anything else here.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Looks like we've reached the center of the workshop...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And still no sign of Coya's baby...

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: Cheep!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Let's search this area for now. If we still can't find Chime, we'll double back.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You split up and begin your search...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #*gasp* Chasca, {NICKNAME}! Come quick!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: What is it? Did you find Chime?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not yet, but look... it's another one of Tepal's notebooks!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Alright.

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: Log No. 428. We decided to restart the experiments on phlogiston refinement, but without telling ██.

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: This is the final obstacle to the success of the Phlogiston Wings project. We cannot fall at the last hurdle!

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: Log No. 436. Earlier today, ██ suggested using qucusaurs as an intermediary to extract refined phlogiston. It's certainly feasible, but...

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: Anyway, as long as our secret experiment succeeds, I'm sure ██ won't bring it up again.

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: Log No. 443. We will conduct the experiment tomorrow. ██ birthday is coming up, so hopefully we'll have a birthday surprise for her.

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: Log No. 444...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why is this log empty?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...I guess whoever wrote down the log number was prevented from recording the results.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's more. Let's keep reading.

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: ...Log No. 0.

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: We lost many comrades in the accident... Among them our friends, lovers, and children...

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: But we cannot stop now. We will keep their legacy alive, and carry their dreams forward.

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: As of today, we are scrapping the artificial refinement method. Instead, we will focus all our efforts on phlogiston extraction from live qucusaurs.

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: They are arrogant beasts whose existence in the wild serves no one but themselves. Their true worth lies in their sacrifice for the sake of human progress.

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: To facilitate our operations, we will gradually move the airborne workshop closer to the Flower-Feather Clan, even as we continue to expand it.

response.speaker: Tepal
response.text: All this, we do to create a world where the skies are for all of humanity to share.

response.speaker: Tepal?
response.text: All this, we do... to make Tepal's dream a reality.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Given the way this is written, not to mention the fact that the numbering has started over from zero... It kinda sounds like this is someone new. Does that mean that Tepal's already...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But in that case, who have we been pursuing?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: There's also a letter tucked into the end of the notebook... It's from Puma.

response.speaker: Puma
response.text: ...Tepal, I don't know where you are right now, so I don't know how to reach you... My best bet is to send this letter to the Flower-Feather Clan.

response.speaker: Puma
response.text: Your father is gravely ill. I know we've had our differences in the past, but he is still your father... Won't you come and visit him, please?

response.speaker: Puma
response.text: I know you never liked him, and cared even less for me... All you've ever yearned for is the sky... and your birth mother.

response.speaker: Puma
response.text: But we'll still be waiting here for you if you do come back. This may be the last chance you'll get to see your father.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Puma's not Tepal's real mom? Huh... Well, she did say he never called her "Mom," but Paimon assumed she was just venting...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: We know that Tepal's father passed away quite recently, and this letter looks recent. By contrast... the writing in this notebook is old and faded.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...It looks like the real reason Tepal didn't attend his father's funeral is because he'd long since passed away himself.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: If we ask ourselves why this letter was sent to the Flower-Feather Clan, why Tepal always yearned for the sky, and how he got his hands on a relic from the Cinder City...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...It all points to one answer.
That's right. Tepal was my child... he was born during my days as a wingless wanderer.
His birth gave me new hope. I wanted to become the kind of mother who spent her days as a valiant rider, soaring the skies... not an aimless, wingless nobody.
But his father wanted to settle down, to give his child a safe, sheltered life in his tribe... We fought about it constantly, until the love we once had for each other was gone.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: He started a new family with another traveler who was also looking to return home... and I went back to the Flower-Feather Clan, alone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Allpa!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: ...I had no idea that despite being raised among the Children of Echoes, my child still harbored dreams of the skies.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Can you imagine, Chasca? The joy and surprise I felt when he showed up at my door, asking to join the flying trials...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Or how proud I was when he said he wanted to prove his own worth, rather than relying on my position as elder...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: ...And then, the anguish that overcame me when he was rejected by the qucusaurs and became wingless, just as I had after my injury...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...You've got a lot of nerve showing your face here.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Heh... Don't take this the wrong way, Chasca. I'm not here for a fight. I just want to talk... isn't that your preferred way to resolve things?

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: I trust you've learned of Tepal's wish on your way here: "a world where the skies are for all of humanity to share."

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: If only his dream can be realized, no one will ever have to lose their wings again. Our aerial prowess will be greater than ever before...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: War will never again come at such a great cost... The loss of Chuychu is a tragedy that need never be repeated.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: So tell me, Chasca... Do you really wish to see the Phlogiston Wings forever grounded and gathering dust?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Nothing you've said excuses all the conflict you've caused.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: You mean the arguments back at the tribe? It was a necessary measure. Sometimes, this is the only way to accelerate the pace of progress.

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: Cheep...!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Is a mother harming her children when she coaxes them into swallowing a bitter pill? Of course not. It is a brief moment of suffering for the greater good, and the child will come to understand this in due course.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: The Phlogiston Wings are that bitter pill. We will never progress as a tribe if we cling to the scraps the Qucusaurs offer us.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Once the people have embraced the Phlogiston Wings, they will never look back — even if they learn how the refined phlogiston is sourced.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: They will convince themselves that the sacrifice of a few qucusaurs is a small price to pay for our dominion over the skies.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: But this I had not anticipated... I barely had the chance to introduce the Phlogiston Wings to the tribe before you found this place...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Your plan was hardly foolproof.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: #Heh... Yet, it can still be salvaged. Chasca, {NICKNAME}, you are the hope of humanity.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: I'm sure you have your doubts about my methods, but know that my love for humanity and for Natlan is genuine.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: You know me, Chasca, and you know that I've always treated everyone in the Flower-Feather Clan as my own children.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: As fellow humans... surely you can understand my perspective?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Quit the quips, this is serious!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Allpa, Natlan doesn't belong to humans alone... and truthfully, neither do I.

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: Cheep...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: How many times has the Abyss invaded Natlan now? And yet despite how much stronger it is than us, Natlan still stands as a nation of humans and saurians.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: "Peace imposed by force will crumble in a matter of days... Because social bonds are what hold a civilization together." Weren't you the one that taught me that?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: And yet, you would break the bond we share with our saurian companions to take more power for ourselves? That's as stupid as hacking your own arm off to use it as a club!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: ...They are wild beasts, driven purely by instinct. How could they possibly understand human social bonds?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... How did someone like her ever become a rider!?

choices.text: Maybe qucusaur instincts are not so different from ours...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Hah, you overestimate them. They bow to the strong and shun the weak — that's all there is to it! They never gave Tepal a second glance when he was at his lowest, nor me when I returned injured from the Cinder City...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: It's all about survival of the fittest for them, plain and simple. They obeyed me once I proved myself stronger than them, but the moment it serves them better, they'll abandon me in a heartbeat!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: You're wrong, Allpa... They only reject the Wingless because they don't want to fly anyone to their death.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Hmph... Chasca, I will promise you this: Only the unruliest wild qucusaurs will be used for phlogiston extraction — the ones who have nothing else to offer to humanity...

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: Cheep...!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Well that's too bad, 'cause I know a few "unruly wild qucusaurs" who don't think that idea's gonna fly. Namely my mom, my sister... and me.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: And the others? To us, they're friends, family, even children... So if you want to put any of them in one of your cages, you're gonna have to go through us!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Is that right? I knew you might be difficult to convince — maybe this will change your mind.

choices.text: ...Because clearly, she had them fooled too.
Then... the benefactor who funded this workshop...
Then... the real ringleader behind all this...
Just in case it gives us any clues on Chime's whereabouts.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: ...Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No... What is she doing!? She'll bring us all down with her!

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: ...But why? We stabilized the relic...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Maybe it got damaged in the fight? If we don't think of something fast, this whole workshop is gonna fall apart!

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: No... They're directly beneath us... My beloved tribe...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If we don't solve this problem at the source...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Okay!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Ugh...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: It's too powerful... This ain't a toy like last time... I don't think I can just throw it aside.

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: Cheep...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: But... But we need to get it far away before it explodes. Then the tribe will be safe, and so will this workshop.

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: ...Cheep?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Coya, remember when we were kids? Come on, let's take this thing high up into the sky.

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: Cheep...!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Don't worry, I know I can get rid of it before it explodes... We're talking some surface wounds at most.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...All I need is for you to catch me at the end. Just like old times.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I can't hold it back anymore, we have to go— Argh!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Don't be insane!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Allpa attacks Chasca from behind while the relic is going wild...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Allpa! What are you...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: You're a fool, Chasca... Why would you choose such a risky solution?

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: We cannot entrust the safety of our tribe to this wild saurian.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I'M the fool!? You really think you can stand a better chance than me?

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Haha... Hahahaha!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Sure, it may be asking too much for an ex-Wingless to escape the blast radius in time.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: But I can fly it a safe distance away... even if it's the last thing I do!

talks.objective: Talk to Chasca and the others

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: So... You're absolutely sure it's not because of the explosion?

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: ....Yes, for the ten-thousandth time, I'm sure. The blast barely touched her. The reason she fainted was old injuries playing up, compounded by over-exertion in recent days...

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: The moment she finally relaxed, all the built-up stress finally caught up with her — and no wonder... Honestly, she's just like you...

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: Anyway. Now you know how we feel when you go off risking life and limb! Your mother and I would both appreciate it if you lived less dangerously... You know she wrote to me from the Masters of the Night-Wind, just to scold me for not doing enough to keep an eye on you?

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: If she wasn't so busy with work, you can bet she'd come back here and chew us both out in person!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...I'll find an opportunity to apologize to her, I promise.

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: You'd better! No more avoiding us, okay? And don't get me started on all the check-ups you've missed...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Got it, got it... Huh... Coya?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...You're awake! I'll... I'll go let everyone know...

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: Hey! But we're not done talking...!

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: *sigh*... What are we gonna do with her, hmm? Even after everything that's happened, she still hasn't figured out how to start the conversation with you...

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: She keeps saying, "I don't think Coya has forgiven me yet"... But if you ask me, she's the one who's scared to open up and have an honest conversation!

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: For all her confidence, she's a very sensitive soul underneath... You'd think as a peacemaker, she of all people would know how to reconcile with her family after a falling out...

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: ...She must have been a handful growing up. Thank you for being there for her.

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: And, of course... Thank you for keeping her safe when you were up there in the sky.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Coya, Uncle Cusco! We're here!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What were you talking about just now?

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: ...Hmph! I was just telling her that she's not to go chasing danger with Chasca ever again!

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Cusco, I understand how you must feel... But it's all thanks to Coya and Chasca's efforts that the airborne workshop didn't come crashing down on our heads.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon almost forgot to ask... They didn't hurt you while we were gone, did they?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Thankfully, when her co-conspirators tried to arrest me, I was out coaching Coyllur and Zhunan.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: The two of them were a huge help. They took care of things while I went around rallying the resistance... So in the end, Allpa's would-be revolt didn't really get off the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: And as it turns out... not all of the Wingless want to see our dear saurian friends replaced with Phlogiston-powered gizmos.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry you got mixed up in this, by the way. We should have caught on to Allpa's scheme sooner... We could have saved so many qucusaurs from getting hurt...

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Most of the airborne workshop has now been dismantled. We've just left one small, harmless part intact... and repurposed it as a jail for Allpa and her cronies.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see how THEY like being locked up in a sky prison!

response.speaker: Cusco
response.text: ...So, it looks like there's just one last conflict left to resolve. Peacemaker, you're up.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...*sigh*

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I said it had to wait until things had blown over, didn't I... And now they have... But I still have no idea what to say.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Coya, I just want to say... I'm sorry for how things went down back then.

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: (There's nothing to be sorry about. Human or saurian, we all grow up, and form new bonds with new family and friends.)

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: (And now, I've come to understand why you chose to stay among the humans.)

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Huh? Does this mean, you're... you're not mad at me anymore?

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: (...That's right.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's that family likeness coming through again...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon... Zip it.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: But... that day, when we ran into each other...

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: (Alright... I admit, I was angry in that moment. I thought you were their accomplice...)

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Huh... So then... when did you finally make your peace with it?

response.speaker: Chime
response.text: (Moooooom!)

response.speaker: Chimpu
response.text: (Hey! Slow down!)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw! It's Chime and Chimpu, they're here too!

response.speaker: Chime
response.text: (Mom, are you okay?)

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: (Mom is fine, love... We're all doing well.)

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: (...I guess it was when... it was my turn to embrace a new family of my own.)

choices.text: Time they got a taste of their own medicine.
